Main Contribution: Proposed an explainable decision support system integrating XGBoost, SHAP, and MCDA scoring with a Streamlit UI.
Limitation: No formal uncertainty calibration, no discrete-event inventory simulation, potential lag leakage in multi-step settings.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Lacks quantitative inventory optimization, multi-horizon causality, and distribution-free uncertainty intervals.
How Our Study Differs: Extends the baseline with direct multi-horizon forecasting, conformal uncertainty, and a full discrete-event inventory simulation.

Main Contribution: Demonstrated massive superiority of GBDTs over statistical and classical ML models on large-scale retail demand.
Limitation: Did not evaluate inventory replenishment, stockouts, or holding costs; focused exclusively on forecast accuracy.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 1 & Gap 4: Forecast accuracy does not establish replenishment decision superiority.
How Our Study Differs: Integrates GBDT multi-horizon forecasts directly into multi-lead-time inventory simulations with holding and shortage costs.

Main Contribution: Introduced the scalable, regularized gradient boosted decision tree algorithm with sparsity-aware splitting.
Limitation: Provides point forecasts only without uncertainty bounds or domain-specific inventory decision logic.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 1 & Gap 3: Point-predictive ML models require calibration layers for operational risk management.
How Our Study Differs: Applies direct XGBoost architectures within a multi-horizon, conformal uncertainty-driven inventory framework.

Main Contribution: Developed a unified framework for interpreting model predictions via cooperative game theory (TreeSHAP).
Limitation: Explains past feature contributions but does not produce forward uncertainty prediction intervals or inventory orders.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 1 & Gap 3: Explanations are descriptive, whereas replenishment requires prescriptive risk margins.
How Our Study Differs: Combines TreeSHAP explanations with conformal non-parametric prediction bounds and inventory simulation.

Main Contribution: Provided a rigorous foundational guide to conformal prediction and finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees.
Limitation: Assumes exchangeability; does not address time-series multi-horizon dependency or inventory decision translation.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 2 & Gap 3: Conformal theory must be adapted to nonstationary time series and multi-horizon replenishment.
How Our Study Differs: Applies rolling forecast-conditional conformal calibration to retail sales time series under distribution shift.

Main Contribution: Proved theoretical coverage degradation bounds for conformal prediction when exchangeability is violated.
Limitation: Theoretical focus; did not evaluate large-scale retail portfolios or multi-period inventory replenishment.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 2: Empirical characterization of conformal coverage degradation in nonstationary time series.
How Our Study Differs: Empirically diagnoses the 2017 retail variance expansion and evaluates scale-normalized conformal intervals in simulation.

Distribution Shift: Yes (Covariate shift with known density ratio)
Main Contribution: Extended conformal prediction to covariate shift where test feature distribution differs from training.
Limitation: Requires known or accurately estimable density ratios; difficult in high-dimensional auto-correlated time series.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 2: Non-parametric scale normalization vs density-ratio weighting in retail forecasting.
How Our Study Differs: Uses point-forecast magnitude as a direct, model-based proxy for localized scale shift in rolling windows.

Main Contribution: Developed conformal prediction algorithms tailored for sequential time-series with RNN backbones.
Limitation: Evaluated on low-dimensional time series; did not examine operational supply chain replenishment decisions.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 3: Bridging time-series conformal prediction with supply chain inventory control.
How Our Study Differs: Integrates multi-horizon conformal upper bounds directly into continuous-review ROP inventory simulation.

Main Contribution: Formulated the Winkler score (interval score) as a proper scoring rule penalizing interval width and coverage violations.
Limitation: Mathematical evaluation metric; does not model supply chain costs, lost sales, or reorder mechanics.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 2: Evaluating interval quality combining width and coverage penalties simultaneously.
How Our Study Differs: Uses Winkler scores to evaluate conformal interval efficiency alongside physical inventory metrics.

Main Contribution: Formulated prescriptive analytics frameworks integrating machine learning feature weights directly into stochastic optimization.
Limitation: Restricted to single-period static optimization; does not model multi-day pipeline tracking or continuous review.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 1 & Gap 3: Prescriptive analytics in multi-day dynamic lead-time replenishment settings.
How Our Study Differs: Simulates dynamic multi-day lead times (L=1..7) with continuous-review ROP and lost sales over a 365-day test horizon.

Main Contribution: Proposed the Big Data Newsvendor, directly mapping high-dimensional features to order quantities via pinball loss.
Limitation: Single-period static model without lead-time inventory pipeline dynamics or multi-horizon rolling review.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 3 & Gap 4: Connecting machine learning with multi-period continuous-review inventory control.
How Our Study Differs: Evaluates multi-horizon forecasts coupled with conformal upper bounds in a continuous-review discrete-event pipeline.

Main Contribution: Demonstrated that directly optimizing quantile forecasts for service levels reduces retail out-of-stock and waste.
Limitation: Used standard pinball loss without conformal calibration; did not evaluate distribution shift or multiple lead times.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 2 & Gap 4: Distribution-free conformal calibration vs. pinball regression across lead times.
How Our Study Differs: Combines direct multi-horizon GBDT with scale-normalized conformal prediction across 4 lead times and 4 penalty levels.

Main Contribution: Demonstrated hybrid ML-statistical architectures for capturing multi-channel retail sales dynamics.
Limitation: Evaluated only point-forecast accuracy without uncertainty bounds or inventory replenishment decisions.
Gap Relevant to Our Study: Gap 1: Machine learning retail forecasting requires decision-level validation.
How Our Study Differs: Evaluates leakage-free forecasting within a complete conformal uncertainty and inventory replenishment framework.

Main Contribution: Comprehensive comparative analysis showing GBDTs outperform LSTMs on structured retail sales data.
Limitation: Focuses strictly on point accuracy without uncertainty quantification or inventory simulation.

Limitation: Did not formulate quantitative safety stock or multi-horizon replenishment algorithms.

How Our Study Differs: Combines explainability with leakage-free multi-horizon forecasting and conformal safety stock sizing.
